scope: OSTEP CPU and scheduling batch against frozen Tycho pages; candidate questions, not claim-level completeness

comparisons.observation: The page correctly says the carrier scheduler is not a backpressure mechanism. OSTEP cache-affinity and queue-topology discussion explains why more runnable tasks do not imply more capacity, but the page does not need to import OS scheduler detail.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.conclusion: The page correctly treats carrier scheduling as a performance mechanism, not a capacity or backpressure contract; OSTEP ch.10 shows cache affinity and queue topology affect scheduling performance without creating capacity.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho uses mean residence time and rejects substituting p99 into Little's Law. OSTEP response time is first-run latency, distinct from completion/turnaround; Tycho's boundary is admission-to-exit, so the metrics should not be conflated.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; name first-response versus completion if OS scheduling is cited.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho uses mean admission-to-exit residence time and rejects substituting p99 into Little's Law. OSTEP distinguishes turnaround (completion) from response time (first run); the two are compatible only when the metric boundary is named.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho discusses serial work, locks, hot keys and coherence. OSTEP adds a concrete single global run-queue lock as a scaling bottleneck and a topology alternative; the page does not currently use a scheduler queue as its example.
comparisons.proposed_action: Optional example only; no measured Tycho scenario exists.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho discusses serial work, locks and coherence but not a single global run-queue lock or queue-topology scaling limit. OSTEP ch.10 supplies a concrete mechanism the page could use as an example; absence is not an error.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: OSTEP list-delete race corroborates the page's claim that coherence and a concurrency-safe collection do not enforce a multi-step business invariant; a lock or atomic transaction still covers the full check-and-commit decision.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.conclusion: The page requires an atomic transaction or state-owner protocol for a multi-step invariant. OSTEP ch.10's list race shows coherence does not enforce compound atomicity; locks cover only the critical section.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: The memory page separates managed heap, native memory, stacks, mappings and RSS. OSTEP address space is a virtual layout, not a resident-set measurement; the two can be compared only with an explicit translation and residency boundary.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; keep virtual size, reserved memory, RSS and live heap separate.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho keeps managed heap, native memory, stacks, mappings and RSS distinct. OSTEP address space is a virtual layout, not a resident-set measurement; the terms should not be mapped one-to-one.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: The diagnostic page keeps GC pauses, RSS growth, native buffers and connection waits separate. OSTEP memory API focuses on allocation ownership, lifetime and invalid frees; those are different failure classes from managed retention and paging.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; the page already avoids treating heap occupancy as diagnosis.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho separates GC pauses, RSS growth, native buffers and connection waits. OSTEP memory API focuses on allocation ownership, lifetime and invalid frees; these are different failure classes.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho describes a VM as a guest-OS/hypervisor isolation boundary. OSTEP process address-space protection is a narrower mechanism inside one OS; the two isolation claims should not be treated as interchangeable.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; name the boundary whenever isolation is claimed.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho describes a VM as a guest-OS/hypervisor isolation boundary. OSTEP process address-space protection is a narrower mechanism inside one OS; the two isolation claims are not interchangeable.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.source_unit: OSTEP chapter 24, Summary Dialogue on Memory Virtualization
comparisons.observation: The latency page decomposes wall-clock time and lists GC, native memory, blocking and dependency waits. OSTEP adds TLB coverage and page-table walk cost as possible memory-stall causes; those are not visible in heap occupancy or GC pause data.
comparisons.proposed_action: Optional addition only when memory stalls do not fit heap or GC evidence.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho's latency hypotheses include JVM/runtime/OS scheduling and native memory but not TLB coverage or page-table walk cost. OSTEP ch.24 adds that diagnostic hypothesis; absence is not a contradiction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho says a JVM-local semaphore cannot serialize writes across replicas and requires a state-owner protocol. OSTEP lock mechanics corroborate the narrower claim that mutual exclusion covers one critical section, not a distributed business invariant.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho correctly limits a JVM-local lock to one process and requires distributed authority for cross-replica invariants. OSTEP ch.28 shows mutual exclusion covers one critical section only.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho explains that publishOn/subscribeOn and boundedElastic move work but do not make a blocking driver asynchronous. OSTEP event-based concurrency shows the same boundary from the OS side: one event loop and nonblocking I/O, with blocking calls as the failure mode.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; keep OS event loop and Reactor scheduler distinct.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho says scheduler choice does not make a synchronous driver nonblocking. OSTEP's event loop shows the same boundary from the OS side: one loop plus nonblocking I/O, with blocking calls as the failure mode.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho asks what is durable when a primary acknowledges. OSTEP journaling makes the same point at the file-system layer: a transaction-end commit and ordered data-before-commit are protocol conditions, not properties implied by writing a log.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; keep acknowledgment, log commit and data durability separate.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho asks what is durable at COMMIT acknowledgment. OSTEP journaling makes the same point at the file-system layer: TxE commit and ordered data-before-commit are protocol conditions, not implied by writing a log.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho distinguishes replica and acknowledgment conditions for durability and availability. OSTEP reliable messaging shows why an acknowledgment can be lost after the effect and why duplicate delivery is a separate problem; exactly-once is conditional, not automatic.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; keep acknowledgment, replication and effect identity separate.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho distinguishes replica and acknowledgment conditions. OSTEP reliable messaging explains lost acknowledgments and duplicate delivery; exactly-once is conditional, not automatic.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho starts from protected outcomes and an explicit threat model. OSTEP connects that stance to OS-controlled resources and the cost of complete mediation; the two are compatible, and neither establishes a specific adversarial capability by itself.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho starts from protected assets, principals and trust boundaries. OSTEP ch.53 grounds the same stance in OS-controlled resources and complete mediation, without establishing a specific adversary capability.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho separates identity, authorization and isolation. OSTEP access control shows the same separation at the reference-monitor level: authentication establishes a principal, authorization decides an access, and the enforcement mechanism has its own cost and revocation limits.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; do not let authentication stand in for authorization.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho separates identity, authorization and isolation. OSTEP access control shows authentication establishes a principal while authorization decides a specific access; the enforcement mechanism has its own cost and revocation limits.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.observation: Tycho separates concurrency-safe data structures from business invariants. OSTEP monitors show that implicit locking still needs a predicate and wake-up discipline; automatic exclusion does not establish the invariant either.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; keep predicate and wake-up protocol explicit.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho separates concurrency-safe structures from business invariants. OSTEP monitors show automatic locking still needs a predicate and wake-up discipline; automatic exclusion does not establish the invariant either.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.source_unit: OSTEP appendix B, Virtual Machine Monitors
comparisons.observation: Tycho treats a VM as a guest-OS/hypervisor isolation boundary. OSTEP adds trap forwarding, double address translation and shadow TLBs as the mechanism behind that boundary; the deployment label alone does not prove the boundary holds.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction; name the hypervisor mechanism in isolation claims.
comparisons.conclusion: Tycho treats a VM as a guest-OS/hypervisor boundary. OSTEP adds trap forwarding, double address translation and shadow TLBs as the mechanism behind it; a deployment label does not prove the boundary holds.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Candidate comparison, not a claim-level audit of the whole page or source.

comparisons.source_unit: JEP 491, Synchronize Virtual Threads without Pinning
comparisons.observation: The page records that the canonical JEP 491 body was not fully accessible during the original research and keeps that limitation as historical provenance. R016 now reads the body: the revised bounded claim matches it, while the LM_LEGACY caveat remains implementation-review-only.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 132-136; JEP 491 Description, residual pinning and diagnostics sections (R016).
comparisons.conclusion: The page claim is consistent with the now-available JEP body. The remaining caveat is about implementation-specific LM_LEGACY behavior, not the JEP text.
comparisons.finding: candidate provenance update, no book edit under #225
comparisons.proposed_action: If the owner later edits the page, cite R016 and retire the inaccessible-body caveat while keeping the LM_LEGACY implementation-review limit.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no implementation inspection or independent review.

comparisons.observation: The page correctly says interruption is a cancellation request, not a rollback. JEP 444 adds a concrete side effect for virtual threads: interrupting socket-blocking I/O closes the socket, so interruption is not a neutral stop for a connection.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 79-83; JEP 444 virtual-thread socket I/O and compatibility sections (R015).
comparisons.conclusion: The page is consistent but does not state the socket-closing side effect; the release boundary matters for JDK 21+ virtual threads.
comparisons.finding: candidate release-boundary addition, no book edit under #225
comparisons.proposed_action: If the owner later edits the page, name the socket-close side effect and the JDK/release boundary.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no socket implementation inspection or execution.

comparisons.source_unit: Overload-control article, concurrency and CoDel sections
comparisons.observation: The page defines a precise queueing boundary and asks when averages can be related by Little's Law. R032 uses in-flight concurrency as an overload signal and reports that static quotas and fixed queue timeouts mis-shed; the two are consistent, but the article is first-party operations evidence.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 59-61; R032 sections Challenges and Building the Foundation.
comparisons.conclusion: The page boundary and the article's concurrency signal are compatible. The article does not supply a general proof that concurrency is always the right signal; it names low-QPS large-write and hot-key exceptions.
comparisons.proposed_action: No edit under #225. If the owner later adds an example, keep the workload and first-party status explicit.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no benchmark or independent review.

comparisons.source_unit: CDC ingestion migration, shadow and reverse-shadow sections
comparisons.observation: The page lists shadow reads and CDC projection as mechanisms with failure conditions. R037 adds a concrete reverse-shadow phase, row-count/checksum equality, latency/resource gates and partition-level bad-data containment. The table is consistent but does not name reverse shadowing or checksum gates.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 51-60; R037 sections The Migration Lifecycle through Rollout and Rollback.
comparisons.conclusion: The page and source agree on the need for side-effect-free comparison and bounded CDC lag. The source adds a reversible reverse-shadow gate that the table could mention as an example.
comparisons.proposed_action: No edit under #225. If the owner later edits the table, consider reverse shadow and checksum gates as one example.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no experiment or independent review.

comparisons.source_unit: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
comparisons.observation: The page says retries at two independent layers can saturate a shared pool even when each retry is below its local maximum, and requires bounded, capacity-aware retry ownership. R060 gives the same warning with the 3^5=243 amplification example and recommends retrying at one layer.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 77; R060 Retries and backoff section.
comparisons.conclusion: The page is consistent with the source and already requires retry ownership, a cumulative budget and safe operation identities.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no experiment or independent review.

comparisons.observation: The page defines control/data planes and says static stability retains pre-existing capacity and local state, while explicitly calling the AWS account a reported design approach rather than a universal orchestration guarantee. R061 supports that bounded claim.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 54; R061 Static stability and patterns sections.
comparisons.conclusion: The page correctly keeps the source claim bounded and does not promise that every orchestrator has the same guarantees.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; no experiment or independent review.

comparisons.observation: The page describes a hedged read as an extra equivalent read after an unexpectedly slow attempt, with an acceptable response and cancellation, and warns that it can double work when a shared dependency is saturated. R065 reports deferred hedges and tied requests with cancellation and bounded extra load.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 83; R065 Within Request Short-Term Adaptations.
comparisons.conclusion: The page accurately states the mechanism and its key limits; the source supports both the tail-reduction claim and the shared-bottleneck caution.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; the reported benchmark is first-party and not re-executed.

comparisons.observation: The page compares Kafka Streams and Flink on state ownership, task migration, changelog restore and operational burden, and marks observed behavior as an evidence gap. R066 documents Kafka Streams local stores, changelog topics, log compaction, standby replicas and rack-aware assignment.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 51-59; R066 Local State Stores and Fault Tolerance.
comparisons.conclusion: The table matches the documented Kafka Streams mechanisms and correctly avoids claiming measured superiority. The source adds standby/rack details that are not in the table, but the table is not wrong.
comparisons.proposed_action: No edit under #225. If the owner later edits the table, consider naming changelog replay and standby state explicitly.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; documentation, not a recovery experiment.

comparisons.observation: The page keeps ISR status, acks=all and min.insync.replicas as separate conditions and warns that a smaller ISR does not preserve the same guarantee. R068 documents ISR commit, acks=0/1/all, min.insync.replicas and the no-loss guarantee only while an ISR replica is alive.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 53; R068 Replication and Availability and Durability Guarantees.
comparisons.conclusion: The page is consistent with the design document and correctly bounds durability by live ISR membership.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; documentation, not a failure experiment.

comparisons.observation: The page says approximate indexes apply filters after the candidate scan, so a restrictive filter can return fewer rows and lower recall, and it names iterative scans, partitioning and partial indexes as mitigations. R069 documents the same post-scan behavior and mitigations.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 52; R069 Filtering and Iterative Index Scans.
comparisons.conclusion: The page accurately states the recall boundary and does not confuse filtering with authorization.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; documentation, not a recall measurement.

comparisons.observation: The page names sums, gauges, histograms and exponential histograms, attribute identity, timestamps and delta/cumulative temporality, and warns that the representations are not interchangeable without conditions. R070 defines those identities, point kinds, temporality and reset semantics.
comparisons.basis: Tycho line 79; R070 Metric Points, Temporality and Resets and Gaps.
comparisons.conclusion: The page accurately summarizes the data-model distinctions and does not treat the formats as equivalent.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; specification, not a backend implementation test.

comparisons.observation: The page says at-least-once queue workers need durable progress and explicit dedup boundaries, and that acknowledging receipt can precede a durable application effect. R071 states that acknowledgements/confirms establish at-least-once, duplicates are possible after retry, and consumers must deduplicate or be idempotent.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 85-94; R071 Acknowledgements and Confirms and Data Safety on the Consumer Side.
comparisons.conclusion: The page correctly separates broker acknowledgement from the consumer durable effect and treats dedup as a correctness boundary.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; documentation, not a delivery experiment.

comparisons.source_unit: RFC 9700, Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
comparisons.observation: The page says a token accepted by one resource should not automatically be reusable at another, and names sender constraints, audience restriction and refresh-token rotation. R072 recommends exactly those measures and explains cross-resource replay.
comparisons.conclusion: The page correctly separates token validity from audience and sender constraints and treats cross-resource reuse as a security failure.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; standards guidance, not an implementation test.

comparisons.observation: The page treats Little's Law as an average identity for a defined boundary and warns against using it to predict tails. R073 shows that finite-interval averages are biased by edge effects and require a statistical estimator, not a direct equality.
comparisons.conclusion: The page and source agree on the mean-only scope. The source adds the finite-interval edge-effect bias, which the page does not spell out; this is an enrichment, not a contradiction.
comparisons.proposed_action: No edit under #225. If the owner later expands the measurement boundary, add the start/end-empty condition and edge-effect caveat.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; paper not reanalyzed and data not rerun.

comparisons.source_unit: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
comparisons.observation: The page requires a client request key scoped to principal/operation, bound to immutable parameters, with atomic token-and-effect storage and expiry tied to client retry horizon. R077 documents a caller-provided request identifier, ACID token-plus-effects, semantically equivalent responses, late arrivals and same-key/different-parameter rejection.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 135-153; R077 Reducing client complexity through Same client request ID.
comparisons.conclusion: The page matches the source contract and adds the client retry-horizon/expiry question. The source does not define a universal API contract, so the page correctly treats it as design evidence.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; first-party article, no execution.

comparisons.observation: The page treats pool capacity as a fleet equation, distinguishes client leases from server connections, and warns that transaction pooling has session-state constraints. R078 defines pool_mode, default_pool_size, max_client_conn, query_wait_timeout and the session-state limits.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 67-80; R078 pool_mode, default_pool_size and dangerous timeouts.
comparisons.conclusion: The page is consistent with the configuration mechanisms and correctly refuses to equate configured pool size with database throughput.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; configuration docs, not a pool benchmark.

comparisons.observation: The page treats pool capacity as a fleet equation and refuses to equate configured pool size with throughput. R079 argues for a small saturated pool, gives the (core*2)+spindles starting point, and explicitly calls sizing deployment-specific.
comparisons.basis: Tycho lines 67-80; R079 The Formula and Caveat Lector.
comparisons.conclusion: The page is consistent with the maintainer guidance and keeps the formula as a starting point, not a universal law.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; guidance, not a benchmark rerun.

comparisons.observation: The page separates permission to reuse, freshness and authorization, and warns that origin failure does not grant permission to expose a response. R075 defines cacheable responses, freshness, validation and the Vary cache key.
comparisons.conclusion: The page matches the caching semantics and keeps authorization outside cache permission.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; standard, not a cache implementation.

comparisons.observation: The page distinguishes connection, stream, attempt and operation identity, and says a GOAWAY last-stream boundary means streams above it were not processed while lower streams may have committed. R076 defines that boundary and request reliability.
comparisons.conclusion: The page accurately states the GOAWAY boundary and does not treat a missing response as rollback.
comparisons.proposed_action: No correction.
comparisons.assessment_limits: Bounded comparison; standard, no network execution.

assessment_summary.note: Assessments are bounded comparisons against the frozen Tycho baseline; they are not independent review, book findings or permission to edit.
